rows.title: Product trial
rows.description: How a product trial runs on the line, from the change record through the lab results and report to the management review.

rows.title: Change record
rows.description: Always the first thing in a product trial. Nothing goes on the line until the change record is through.
rows.quote: Nothing goes on the line until the change record is through.
assumed: Priya's write-up and Tom Baker's sign-off grouped as one stage, since the notes treat the change record as one thing
'Through', 'done' and 'complete' all read as meaning signed off by Tom Baker

rows.title: Write the change record
rows.description: Priya writes it up. She uses last year's form and attaches the supplier's safety sheet.
rows.quote: she spends about thirty hours on it over two weeks
assumed: 'two weeks' read as 10 workdays
'about thirty hours' read as 30 hours in all, for Priya
'Priya' read as Priya Shah, the only Priya on the list

rows.title: Approval: Change record
rows.description: Tom Baker signs off the change record. Give it a week, more if he is travelling.
rows.quote: Then Tom Baker signs it off, give that a week, more if he's travelling.
assumed: 'a week' read as 5 workdays
'Then' with no gap said read as starting the day Priya's write-up ends (0 workdays after)
'Tom Baker' written as heard; the people list has Tom Becker (Planner), and I did not assume they are the same person

rows.title: Tell the supplier the trial dates
rows.description: Tyler tells the supplier the dates so the material shows up in time.
rows.quote: Two days after the change record's done, Tyler tells the supplier the dates
assumed: 'Two days' is a bare 'days', read as 2 workdays
The change record has subtasks, so the tie is to its last one, the approval
'Tyler' read as Tyler Nguyen, the only Tyler on the list

rows.title: Train each shift on the new work instruction
rows.description: Mike trains each shift on the new work instruction, a couple of hours a day for three days, finishing the day before the trial window starts.
rows.notes:
- [ ] Book the break room
- [ ] Print the work instruction
- [ ] Get each shift's sign-off
rows.quote: a couple of hours a day for three days, finishing the day before the trial window starts
assumed: 'a couple of hours' read as 2 hours a day
'three days' read as 3 workdays
'the day before' read as 1 workday before the start of the trial window
'Mike' read as Mike Ortiz, the only Mike on the list

rows.title: Trial window
rows.description: Day shift only. Priya and Mike are both on it. Operations leads each day's start-up.
rows.notes:
- [ ] Confirm operators are trained
- [ ] Confirm the lab is booked for samples
rows.quote: has to run five days after the change record is complete
assumed: 'five days after' is a bare 'days', read as 5 workdays
'five days long' read as 5 workdays
The change record has subtasks, so the tie is to its last one, the approval
'about six hours a day' read as 6 hours a day for each of Priya and Mike
plant_event set because a trial is a run on the line that others plan around; this was inferred, not said

rows.title: Lab tests the samples
rows.description: The lab lead gets to the samples the day after the run is over and the samples have shipped. Test adhesion and gloss on every batch. If gloss is out of range a second run might be needed; nobody has decided who calls that.
rows.quote: the lab lead gets to them the next day
assumed: 'the next day' read as 1 workday after the end of the trial window
The step also waits on the samples having shipped, which is not a row, so the tie is to the end of the trial window only
'the lab lead' is a job title with no name, so it stays in the description

rows.title: Write the report
rows.quote: it takes about a week, starting a couple of days after the lab's done
assumed: 'You write the report' read as me, the person asking, so the assignee is Me
'about a week' read as 5 workdays
'a couple of days' read as 2 workdays

rows.title: Management review
rows.description: A management review of the trial, held a week after the report. No attendees were named.
rows.quote: a management review a week after the report
assumed: 'a week after the report' read as 1 week after the end of the report
Treated as a meeting, not an approval, because nobody said it has to approve anything before work goes on

rows.title: Safety team review
rows.description: Somebody from the safety team has to look at it. When, how long and who are not known yet.
rows.quote: Somebody from the safety team has to look at it at some point too
assumed: Placed last because no point in the sequence was given
'it' is not clear (the change record, the trial or the report)
Safety label applied because the review is by the safety team
'the safety team' has no named person, so it stays in the description
